memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "That night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two female servants and his eleven sons and crossed the ford of the Jabbok. After he had sent them across the stream, he sent over all his possessions. So Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him till daybreak." - Gen 32:22-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob sends his family and everything he owns across the Jabbok stream, and then a striking phrase appears: "So Jacob was left alone." On the night before the most frightening day of his life, Jacob is by himself in the dark. And it is precisely there, in his solitude, that God comes to meet him — "a man wrestled with him till daybreak."

There is something significant in Jacob being left alone. All his life, Jacob had relied on his own cleverness, his schemes, his ability to manage people and outcomes. Now everything and everyone is removed. His wives, his children, his wealth, his plans — all sent across the river. There is nothing left between Jacob and God but Jacob himself.

Sometimes God brings us to a place of solitude to meet us there. When the noise dies down, the distractions are stripped away, and we are finally alone, we can encounter God in ways the crowded, busy life never allows. The lonely night can become holy ground.

If God has led you into a season of solitude — a sleepless night, a quiet struggle, a place where you feel utterly alone — do not despair. He may be drawing you aside precisely so He can meet with you. Some of our deepest encounters with God happen when we are, at last, left alone with Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do I respond to seasons of solitude — with dread or openness?
2. Could God be drawing me aside to meet with Him?
3. What might God want to do in me when I am finally alone with Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, in my lonely nights and quiet struggles, meet with me. Strip away my distractions and self-reliance, and draw me aside to encounter You. Amen.
